title: Fetters of Destiny
next_chapter_hook: The stakes the imperial emissary raised far exceeded imagination, and the sealed text deep within the Tianji Record seemed to come alive. Chen Ji sensed a gaze from Heaven itself piercing through the void—in the next instant, the entire Tianqing Sect seemed shrouded by an invisible force.

text.content: Night dark as ink, in the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain Servants' Quarters, Chen Ji sat alone on a meditation cushion, the fragment before him faintly glowing. Since that day he reached an agreement with Ye Qing, he had not used the Tianji Record to peer into the future for seven days—every consumption of the Heavenly Fate Value was shortening the time until he could reunite with his sister. Sudden hurried footsteps came from outside the window, Chen Ji's brow furrowed slightly, yet he did not open his eyes, merely letting his fingertips lightly brush the fragment's edge as he murmured softly: "They've come." His tone was so calm it seemed he had long foreseen this scene.

dialogue.content: (The remnant soul quivered slightly, speaking at extreme speed) Master, they've come. From the imperial court, tearing through space directly—this shows their desperation far exceeds your expectations. Moreover, the visitor's aura runs deep and unfathomable, definitely not an ordinary official.

text.content: Before the words even finished, the wooden door of the servants' quarters had silently turned to dust. Chen Ji raised his eyes to see a figure in a玄 black official robe stepping in under the moonlight, surrounded by faint golden dragon patterns—that was the mark of imperial luck bestowed upon one. The visitor appeared middle-aged, with an elegant face yet carrying an undeniable pressure, his gaze sweeping over Chen Ji's worn servant robe, the corners of his mouth lifting slightly.

dialogue.content: (The visitor stood with hands clasped behind, his voice low yet vibrating the roof tiles) Chen Ji, servant disciple of the Tianqing Sect? This official comes bearing the emperor's decree for one purpose—the imperial court has intelligence concerning "Chen Tianming," confirmed he still walks among the living.

text.content: Chen Tianming—that was Chen Ji's father's name, everyone believed he had long died in that sect war ten years ago. Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply, yet the next instant he restored that wooden expression, only his fingers resting on his knee tightening slightly. The three characters "陈天命" were like a blunt blade, slowly and firmly piercing the softest part of his heart. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang in his mind, carrying unprecedented gravity: "Master, this person speaks with deception, the imperial court's involvement in this matter must have deeper meaning. But... this might also be a lead to finding the young miss."

dialogue.content: (Rising slowly, movements sluggish yet hiding sharp edges) The imperial court's intelligence... I wonder what the大人 wishes me to exchange for it?

(A slight laugh, gaze like a blade) Exchange? What could you possibly have to exchange? This official comes bearing an imperial decree to bestow fortune. The evidence that Tianqing Sect's old sect master Ling Yuan colluded with the Demonic Path—the imperial court already possesses seventy percent. If you're willing to appear as the "witness," these pieces of evidence shall belong to you. Then the Tianqing Sect will be without a leader, and you—this废柴 servant—will become the key chess piece to reshape the sect's landscape.

text.content: Chen Ji lowered his head to look at his own palms, covered in calluses, as if observing something unrelated to himself. The imperial court wanted him as a chess piece—this was not surprising, what truly shocked him was how certain they were that he would agree. Just as he was about to speak, the Tianji Record fragment suddenly vibrated violently, and an unseen sealed character emerged from deep within the paper, squirming like a living thing: "The executor's fate is the covenant of destiny, the contract is established once, the cycle never ceases."

dialogue.content: (The remnant soul was terrified to the extreme, voice trembling) This... this is the activation condition for the seventh-layer seal! Master, the Tianji Record is saying—you are not choosing to become the executor, but were born so! From the moment you obtained this fragment, fate was already locked!

text.content: Chen Ji abruptly clenched the fragment, his knuckles white. Those words continued to slowly emerge, each stroke branding his consciousness like a searing iron. He suddenly understood—the Tianji Record's every prophecy was pushing him toward that destined final outcome. The death prophecy in Chapter Seven Hundred was not a warning, but part of the contract. He had never been a chess player; from beginning to end, he was the executor selected by the eye of heaven. The imperial emissary seemed to sense something, his brow creasing.

dialogue.content: (Stepping forward,语速suddenly放缓) Chen Ji, this official knows what concerns you. But understand—the imperial court only wants a witness. Your father's whereabouts, your sister's location, even... the secrets behind your incomplete Tianji Record, we can all discuss.

text.content: Sister. Chen Ji's heart was struck violently. Chen Nian, that girl taken by the Holy Sect, who became the "Heavenly Fate Lock Key"—her existence interfered with the Tianji Record's foresight—any scene with her in it was blurred. How would the imperial court know this? Unless... they were themselves another force in heaven's chess game. Mo Xiansheng's silence was more alarming than any words to Chen Ji, meaning even this remnant soul who knew all the truth of the Tianji Record did not dare to rashly judge at this moment.

choice.prompt: The stakes the imperial emissary dangled were tantalizing beyond measure—his father's whereabouts, his sister's clues, even Ling Yuan's handle. However, there has never been a free lunch in this world, Chen Ji had to make a choice in this invitation that was clearly a game of fate.

choices.text: Temporarily agree, act according to circumstances.
choices.description: First accept the leads provided by the imperial court, use them to investigate his father's and sister's whereabouts, while secretly gathering imperial court intelligence, seeking an opportunity to break the局.
choices.visible_cost: Owe the imperial court a favor, may expose more information.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain intelligence of Chen Tianming's survival and Chen Nian's clues.
choices.risk_hint: The imperial court may thereby control Chen Ji's movement trajectory.

dialogue.content: (Slightly lowering his head, assuming a respectful posture) This one is merely a servant, what virtue do I possess to merit the imperial court's regard? But if it means finding leads about my father and younger sister, Chen Ji... is willing to try.

text.content: Upon hearing this, the imperial emissary's eyes flickered with a barely detectable look of satisfaction, then took a jade slip from his sleeve and extended it toward Chen Ji. The jade slip's surface was carved with nine five-clawed golden dragon patterns, the highest rank token of the imperial court—with this slip, Chen Ji could mobilize any imperial covert operative along his path. Mo Xiansheng sighed lightly in his consciousness: "Master, this slip contains tracking restrictions, once activated, your whereabouts will be completely transparent to the imperial court."

choices.description: Refuse to be anyone's chess piece, reject the imperial court's transactional invitation. Even if the clues are tempting, Chen Ji refuses to become a manipulated chess piece—even if the other party is part of heaven's chess game.
choices.visible_cost: Lose the opportunity to obtain intelligence, may offend the imperial court.
choices.visible_reward: Maintain freedom of action, unconstrained by any contract
choices.risk_hint: The imperial envoys will not necessarily let this matter rest

dialogue.content: (Slowly settling back onto the meditation cushion, his expression as indifferent as ever) Thank you for your kindness, sir. It is merely that Chen Ji is naturally dull-witted and understands nothing of chessboard schemes. I'm afraid I will disappoint the Empire's expectations.

text.content: The envoy's expression instantly darkened, a dangerous glint flickering through those scrutinizing eyes. The air seemed to crystallize for a moment before he rearranged his smile, though this time the warmth failed to reach his gaze. 'Interesting.' he murmured. 'Chen Ji, this official will remember you.' With that, he swept his sleeve and departed, pausing briefly at the threshold. 'By the way, your sister has not been faring well at the Holy Sect—I do hope that when we meet again, you will have reconsidered.'

choices.description: Remaining non-committal, using histrash杂役 identity to probe the envoy's true intentions. Since the Empire took the initiative to approach him, there must be more secrets untold—Chen Ji intends to force them to reveal their hand first.
choices.visible_cost: May arouse the envoy's suspicion, leading to a passive position
choices.visible_reward: Obtain deeper insider information regarding the relationship between the Eye of Heavenly Secrets and the Tianji Record
choices.risk_hint: Excessive probing may expose that Chen Ji is not truly atrash

dialogue.content: (Blinking with feigned bewilderment) I don't quite understand what you're saying, sir. Executors? Predestined contracts? This humble one only knows how to chop wood and carry water every day. May I ask what exactly this 'witness' you mentioned is supposed to do?

text.content: The envoy stared into Chen Ji's eyes for a long moment, as if trying to discern whether any hidden sharpness lay beneath that wooden expression. After a pause, he laughed lightly, 'You are quite cautious. Very well, allow this official to elaborate—the Eye of Heavenly Secrets selects an 'Executor' every thousand years to cleanse those whose fate has become chaotic. Your fellowtrashdisciple Han Lie from Tianqing Sect, has he not recently had some connection with you?' Mo Xiansheng gasped within Chen Ji's consciousness: 'Master, he is implying that Han Lie is also a piece on the board!'

Chen Ji's expression remained unchanged, yet within his heart, monstrous waves raged. Han Lie—that Xuanwu Sect genius he had repeatedly suppressed with his foresight ability, only to watch him grow stronger with each defeat. Did the Empire truly know about the entanglement between Han Lie and himself? More critically, the information embedded in the envoy's words: the Eye of Heavenly Secrets selects one Executor every thousand years. What did this mean? It meant he was not the only piece selected, and the Tianji Record was certainly not the only copy in existence.
(Chen Ji raised his head, his voice terrifyingly calm) Regarding this 'Executor' you speak of, sir, might I inquire—what consequences await should I refuse this 'predestined contract'?

Upon hearing this, the envoy's expression grew subtle. He did not answer immediately, but instead walked slowly to the window, gazing toward the Tianqing Sect Main Peak. Beneath the moonlight, that mist-shrouded peak resembled a slumbering beast. 'Consequences?' he murmured softly. 'The last Executor to refuse was the Sect Master of the Qinglian Sword Sect three hundred years ago. He believed he could defy destiny and alter his fate, but... care to guess the outcome?' Chen Ji gripped the fragment upon his knee tightly, his knuckles white. Mo Xiansheng's voice whispered in his mind: 'Master, the Qinglian Sword Sect... has now become a historical footnote.'

The envoy turned, the moonlight casting a cold silhouette behind him. He suddenly smiled, that grin carrying an inexplicable quality. 'Chen Ji, you are an intelligent person, and this official will not beat around the bush with you. The Eye of Heavenly Secrets' chess game has already been set. You are a piece, not a player—this was determined the moment of your birth. The Empire's advantage lies in the fact that we at least offer our pieces some... dignified choices. As for your sister who was taken by the Holy Sect...' He paused. 'Have you ever pondered why she was chosen as the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key'?'

dialogue.content: (In his mind, the young face of Chen Nian surfaces, those eyes identical to his own shining vividly in the darkness) Brother, Nian'er is not afraid. Nian'er will wait for you to come take me home...

text.content: Chen Ji abruptly closed his eyes, a barely audible hoarse sound rolling in his throat. When he opened them again, those eyes had regained their customary composure, though the veins on the hand gripping the fragment twitched slightly. 'What you mean is...' His voice was very soft. 'My sister was chosen by the Eye of Heavenly Secrets?' The envoy shook his head. 'No, she was chosen to restrain you. The Heavenly Fate Lock Key does not lock the Tianji Record—it locks you. Every time you use your foresight ability, she moves one step closer to death.'

choice.prompt: The words of the imperial envoy pierced like a blade into Chen Ji's deepest wound—the very existence of his sister was a sword of death suspended above his head. The impact of this truth upon Chen Ji far exceeded imagination.

choices.text: Suppress sorrow and rage, maintain rationality
choices.description: Forcefully contain the shock and fury,不让 the envoy perceive any weakness. Since his sister's fate is bound to his own abilities, the use of the Tianji Record must become infinitely more cautious.
choices.visible_cost: Psychological pressure intensifies dramatically, potentially giving rise to heart demons
choices.visible_reward: Maintain the disguise, do not expose vulnerabilities
choices.risk_hint: Repressing emotions carries a price; accumulating to a critical threshold will inevitably erupt

text.content: Chen Ji slowly unclenched his fingers gripping the fragment, his palm already a mess of blood and torn flesh. He gazed at the ravaged wooden floor, the corners of his mouth twisting into a bitter arc. 'So that's how it is.' His voice was very soft, as if discussing something that had nothing to do with him. 'Thank you for informing me, sir.' The envoy raised an eyebrow, seemingly unprepared for such a reaction. 'Is that all?' Chen Ji lifted his gaze, those pitch-black pupils revealing absolutely no emotional fluctuation. 'Then what reaction would you like to witness from me, sir?'

choices.text: Press for the truth, regardless of exposure
choices.description: No longer concealing anything, he questioned the envoy about more information regarding his sister. Since the other party had already shown their cards, Chen Ji also wanted to negotiate for more leverage—even if it meant revealing that he was not truly atrash.
choices.visible_cost: Exposing strength might invite even greater targeted attacks
choices.visible_reward: Obtain more critical intelligence about Chen Nian
choices.risk_hint: Letting the Imperial Court realize Chen Ji's true value would lead to unpredictable consequences

dialogue.content: (Rising abruptly, his surrounding aura suddenly transforming) Enough! Chen Nian is not your bargaining chip, nor is she some kind of Heavenly Fate Lock! Tell me—how do I save her?

text.content: The envoy froze for a moment, then burst into laughter. That laugh was particularly harsh in the silent night, echoing through the dilapidated Servants' Quarters. "Interesting!" He收敛 his smile, his gaze sharp as a blade, "So even thetrash servant of the Tianqing Sect has some fire in him. But Chen Ji, the more you act like this, the more it proves you're worth taking seriously. Want to save your sister? Fine, first prove you're worthy of this bargain." He took out another Jade Slip from his sleeve, "This is the final message left by your father Chen Tianming—take it, as a gesture of good faith."

Chen Ji took the second Jade Slip, and the moment his fingertips touched the warm jade, a familiar aura rushed toward him. It was his father's unique presence—warm, steady, like those rough yet warm big hands from his childhood memories. Mo Xiansheng's voice sounded, with a slight tremor: "Master, this is real... The aura of Senior Chen Tianming does indeed exist within this Jade Slip." Chen Ji closed his eyes, forcibly suppressing the surging emotions. The Jade Slip contained a fragment of spiritual consciousness imprint, requiring at least a Golden Core stage spiritual consciousness intensity to decipher—another threshold set by the Imperial Court.

(Pocketing the Jade Slip, his voice returning to calm) The Imperial Court's sincerity, I've received. But there's still something I don't understand—what exactly does the Heavenly Eye want the Executor to do? What's the connection between the death prophecy in Chapter 700 and this "Fate Agreement"?

The envoy fell silent for a moment, as if considering how much to reveal. Finally, he spoke, his voice low as if emerging from an abyss: "The Heavenly Eye is a fragmented existence of Heavenly Will. It doesn't maintain just one person's fate, but the balance of order throughout the entire cultivation world. Whenever a variable appears that could overturn the entire situation—like the Tianji Record in your hands—it activates the 'Chess Game Purification' program. The Executor's task is to personally destroy those forces that 'shouldn't exist.'" He stared directly into Chen Ji's eyes, "And the reason you can see the death prophecy in Chapter 700 is because that's precisely the sign that the contract takes effect. Once you fully awaken, the Executor identity will be completely locked in—at which point..." He didn't finish, but the unspoken implications were already clear enough.

Chen Ji suddenly smiled, that smile very faint, yet carrying an inexplicable chill. "So, the Heavenly Eye wants to use my hand to destroy the Tianji Record? It chose me, not because I have anything special, but because... I'm the most suitable 'tool'." The envoy didn't deny it, just looked at him meaningfully, "Isn't it possible for a tool to become a chess player? Three thousand years ago, that supreme expert who overthrew the old order was initially nothing more than a piece in the Heavenly Chess Game." He walked toward the door again, "In three days, this official will come again. At that time, give this official an answer—do you accept fate, or..." He didn't finish, his figure already vanishing into the night.

Night wind poured through the broken doors and windows, rustling the fragmented pages. Chen Ji stood alone before the window, gazing toward where the Imperial Court envoy had disappeared, his eyes dark as an abyss. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out in his consciousness, carrying rare heaviness: "Master, the choice you now face is more dangerous than this old servant anticipated. Accept the Imperial Court, and you'll become a puppet of the Heavenly Eye; reject the Imperial Court, and the Tianqing Sect and everyone you care about will be buried. What's even more terrifying is..." He paused, "No matter how you choose, the death prophecy in Chapter 700 is destined to occur. The only difference is whether you'll face death as an 'Executor' or as a 'rebel.'"

Chen Ji slowly turned around, tucking the fragment into his chest. In that moment, all pretense fell away from his face, revealing that true countenance that had been suppressed for too long—not dull, not cowardly, but an almost cold determination. "Remember grudges without being rash" was his creed, "knowing how to subvert the expected" was his instinct. Since the Heavenly Eye viewed him as a tool, he would become a blade that could bite back at its master. He murmured: "Three days? Enough." Mo Xiansheng was stunned, "Master has already made a decision?" Chen Ji didn't answer, merely calculating his next move in his heart. The Imperial Court, Ling Yuan, the Holy Sect, the Heavenly Eye—all his enemies were in the open, while he alone remained hidden. This was his greatest advantage. As long as this trump card remained unplayed, he still had the possibility of turning the tables.

When the eastern sky began to lighten, Chen Ji finally snapped out of his contemplation. He looked down at the two Jade Slips in his chest—one carved with nine dragon patterns, representing the Imperial Court's bargaining chip; the other warm and smooth as ever, carrying his father's final breath. He gently stroked that testament letter from his father, his fingertips trembling slightly. "Father..." he softly called out, his voice carrying a vulnerability he had never shown before others. A moment later, that trace of vulnerability vanished without a trace, replaced by his usual composure and coldness. He stood up and walked toward the door, the morning light stretching his shadow long. The three-day deadline would arrive in an instant. And he had to find a way to break the局 within these three days.
